title: Pin Oak: Ancient Pin Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A North American swamp oak with a drooping crown and scarlet fall colour. See the three Pin Oaks mapped so far, from 1840s Haarlem to 1910s Sittard.
intro:
Pin oak is a North American swamp species, native to wet bottomland from the Great Lakes down through the Mississippi valley, that reached European gardens at the start of the nineteenth century and became a Dutch park favourite decades later. Three are mapped so far: an 1840s planting in Haarlem's Frederikspark, one from the 1860s in Apeldoorn's Oranjepark, and a 1910s specimen in Sittard's Stadspark.

It is easy to place once you have seen one. The lower branches sweep down toward the grass while the upper ones reach up, and the leaves are cut into narrow, bristle-tipped lobes far sharper than any native oak's. The name comes from the small pin-like stubs of dead branchlets along the trunk, not the leaves. All three hold their scarlet October colour and their dead leaves well into winter, so a pin oak is often the last oak in a park still dressed.
